senses.sense_definition: The quality of being brief, clear, and direct in speech or writing; conciseness.

examples.text: The editor commended the article for its clarity and remarkable <w>concision</w>.
He managed to explain the complex scientific theory with admirable <w>concision</w>.

senses.sense_definition: A form of media constraint or censorship where nuanced discussions are compressed to fit tight broadcast time slots.

examples.text: Critics argue that structural media <w>concision</w> prevents complex political viewpoints from being explored properly.
The constraints of television <w>concision</w> often reduce intricate debates to snappy soundbites.

senses.sense_definition: A cutting off, division, or schismatic faction.

examples.text: The doctrinal disputes eventually caused a bitter <w>concision</w> among the members of the church.
Historical texts describe a radical <w>concision</w> that split the ruling assembly into rival factions.

traits.comment: Used historically or in archaic prose

senses.sense_definition: The act of cutting up or mutilating; mutilation.

examples.text: Ancient legal texts warned against the severe bodily <w>concision</w> inflicted upon captured deserters.
The cruel rites involving deliberate physical <w>concision</w> were abolished centuries ago.

traits.comment: Used in archaic descriptions of bodily mutilation

senses.sense_definition: Mutilation of the flesh, specifically used as a derogatory term for mere physical circumcision.

examples.text: In his letter, the apostle warned the faithful to beware of the <w>concision</w>.
The term <w>concision</w> was employed polemically to mock ritual circumcision lacking inward faith.
